differential_ui_check.method: Visible control inventory captured in Chromium for the built port and for the pinned source harness, then compared as sets
differential_ui_check.differences: All boot and settings differences are data or user configuration, not UI surface: session titles and counts, selected model id, and the access-mode, agent-mode and busy-enter labels. The port renders Full access, Code mode and Steer because ~/.seekdeep/settings.yaml sets permission.defaultPreset: danger-full-access, agent-presets.default: code and ui-conversation.busyEnter: steer; the source home sets none of those and shows its own defaults. payload_and_transport_work_verified_here: Shipped WebAssembly carries no DWARF: the 46 browser artifacts fall from 419 MiB to 69.7 MiB, and the largest artifact (5.7 MiB) is below the browser's 8 MiB synchronous compile limit. The Chromium fixture that maps a real wasm panic frame to Rust source through client_bg.wasm.map still passes.
Cold page load 20.9 MB and reload 1.2 MB; Host CPU per page load 2.06 s cold, then 0.15 s once the encoded body is replayed for a revision-addressed target.
Lossless JSON string conversion decodes and encodes runs instead of characters: to_utf16 1,925 ms to 46 ms and encode_utf16 below the sampling threshold on one cold session open.

A Definition's run of update Matches folds in one call: one decode, every Match applied against the state the previous one left, one encode. Measured per plugin module over one cold open of the same session, ui-conversation 1,545 ms to 1,380 ms, ui-trajectory 1,244 ms to 1,074 ms, client total 4,970 ms to 4,630 ms and the open 4,856 ms to 4,528 ms, two runs per side holding to about 0.2%. Verified afterwards by the same keyless run and navigation gate listed above.

A literal ASCII run decodes to UTF-16 one unit per byte instead of dispatching on each character's encoded width. `extend_desugared` under `JsonRef::to_utf16` falls from 266 ms to 62-76 ms per cold open, ui-conversation from 1,380 ms to 1,354 ms and ui-trajectory from 1,073 ms to 1,049 ms.
remaining: The client's per-event cost is the whole gap, and no localized item measured over rounds 4-6 exceeds 1-2% of an open. Closing it means changing what crosses the wasm boundary per event, which has no counterpart in the source: the source keeps session data as JavaScript values and converts nothing.

The steering keyless scenario times out under CPU contention: its 10 s poll is generous for the source and tight for a client that renders about ten times slower. It passes in isolation and in an undisturbed full run, so it is load-induced flakiness rather than a port defect, and it is a consequence of the gap above.

A cold session open of an 8 MB history is 4.59 s against the source harness's 0.48 s on the same payload. The Host serves the history in 335 ms, so the cost is the client: 36,196 assistant/chunk events are each marshalled through JSON text into WASM and back. Per module over one open: ui-conversation 1,339 ms, ui-trajectory 1,049 ms, client-runtime 635 ms, frames carrying no script URL 465 ms, idle 393 ms, program 171 ms. Every remaining item measured is 1-2% of the open, so the gap is not reachable by further localized work.
Routing container values to the browser's own JSON parser instead of materializing a serde tree first was implemented and measured at no change in open time, then reverted.

The 33 source goldens this suite does not produce belong to scenarios driven by other xtask gates (web-assembled, web-workspaces, web-settings, web-models-settings, web-plugin-settings, web-onboarding, web-assembled-snapshots), which were not run here.
Full workspace Clippy, full workspace tests and cargo xtask parity were not run in this checkpoint; no repository-wide parity claim is made.
measurement_note: Wall clock at the 5-10% level is not measurable on this machine while another session compiles: the same committed source measured 4.29-4.62 s and later 4.63-5.04 s. Changes of this size are resolved by per-plugin-module profile self-time instead, where two runs of the same build hold to about 0.2%.

differential_client_cost.method: The same visible session opened in the built port and in the pinned source harness, capturing each history payload and profiling the browser

content_arrival.source_harness: 65,137 characters of conversation at 465 ms after the click
content_arrival.port: 607 characters until 3,837 ms, then 9,598 characters at 4,538 ms

differential_client_cost.conclusion: The two implementations ship comparable payloads and the port ships fewer events than the source. Both publish the window atomically, so the port shows an empty conversation pane for about 3.9 s where the source shows content at once. The gap is a per-event constant in the client, not a payload, pagination or publication-strategy difference.

trajectory_share.method: The same session opened in the built port with the trajectory plugin enabled and disabled through a launcher patch overlay that sets disabled on the ui-trajectory row
trajectory_share.chat_output: 9,598 characters with the plugin and 9,582 without; the 16-character difference is exactly the Chat and Trajectory tab labels it provides
trajectory_share.conclusion: The trajectory Definitions cost about 1.4 s of a 4.5 s cold open, roughly 30 per cent, and contribute nothing to the Chat pane the user is looking at. The module profile shows the same shape as ui-conversation: per-event JSON scanning and UTF-16 conversion.
trajectory_share.why_the_obvious_fix_is_not_taken: Registering those Definitions lazily on first Trajectory use would route through rebuild_registry, which re-folds the entire stored window with every Definition, so the first Trajectory open would pay the whole 3-4.5 s again. Capturing this saving needs an assembler capability that folds the stored window for one newly registered Definition, plus a background fold after the first paint. That is a product trade, not a localized fix: the Chat pane would appear about 1.4 s sooner, and the ledger would either fill in behind it or stall the first Trajectory open.

gates_note: Every web gate this repository exposes has now been run against the current tree: 14 gates, all passing. No feature bug was found by exercising them.
idle_explained: The 393 ms idle bucket in a cold open is predominantly the history round trip: the Host's response latency is 335 ms and the client cannot fold the window before the whole document arrives. The slice yields are not the cost, because the defer is a browser timer and 18 slices at 2,048 events cost about 4 ms each.
